title: Pawprint deployment configuration
description: Validates both config/deploy.defaults.json (upstream-owned, never edited by adopters) and config/deploy.config.json (adopter-owned overrides). Both files share this shape; every field is optional so an override file may be minimal. Resolution order is builtin < defaults file < override file < environment variable < CLI flag.

configVersion.description: Schema contract version. A major mismatch is a hard failure; run 'pawprint config migrate' to upgrade.

scenarios.description: Scenario catalogue for repositories that publish one. Keys are scenario ids; the values carry the human-facing metadata a report renders. The scenario's own manifest, not this, is the authority on what it deploys.

environments.description: Per-environment overrides layered on top of defaults. Keys are environment names; 'dev' and 'prod' are conventional.

repositoryReference.description: Either a full URL or the owner/repo shorthand. Both are unambiguous and both are already in use across the organisation.

noSecretKeys.description: Configuration files are committed to source control. Secret-shaped keys are rejected outright; runtime secrets belong in Key Vault, pipeline identity in GitHub Environment variables. JSON Schema uses ECMA-262 regex with no inline case-insensitive flag, so this pattern covers the conventional camelCase and snake_case spellings. Keys that merely name, count or toggle a secret are metadata and are exempt. The resolver additionally applies a case-insensitive check and produces the actionable error message.

connectors.description: Which connectors are enabled and at which permission tier. Tiers are cumulative and defined in config/connectors.catalog.json. Choose the lowest tier that unlocks what you actually need.

dns.description: Optional external DNS authority used only to verify and route a custom domain. Credentials are runtime secrets and never belong here.

zoneName.description: Authoritative Cloudflare DNS zone, for example example.com.

secrets.description: Where this service's runtime secrets live. Default is none: a service with no secrets should not provision a vault, and most do not have any. Key Vault costs almost nothing at rest, so consolidation is never a cost decision; it is a blast-radius decision.

mode.description: none: no vault and no grants. workload: this repository deploys and owns a vault in its own resource group, so the vault's lifetime matches the service's. platform: the shared tier 0 vault holds the secrets and this service is granted read access scoped to named secrets only, never to the whole vault.

vaultName.description: Workload vault name. Azure caps this at 24 characters.

platformVaultName.description: Tier 0 vault the named secrets are read from. Owned by pawprint, not by this repository.

secretNames.description: Secrets this service reads. Each one becomes an individually scoped role assignment, which is what keeps a shared vault safe to share.

purgeProtection.description: Azure cannot turn this off once enabled, and it reserves the vault name for the whole soft-delete window. Ephemeral or frequently rebuilt workloads should leave it false.

expirationDays.description: Expiry stamped on rotated secrets. A secret with no expiry is a secret nobody ever rotates.

warningDays.description: How long before expiry the audit starts warning.

approvedSubscriptions.description: Allowlist of subscription ids Pawprint may deploy into. Enforced at preflight: a subscription absent from this list is refused before any resource is touched. Absent or empty means nothing is approved, so it fails closed.

sinks.description: Where emitted pawprints are written. JSON is always the on-the-wire format; sinks decide durability. Multiple sinks may be active at once.

file.description: Local filesystem. Always available, including air-gapped. Not durable beyond the machine.

archive.description: Keep timestamped copies of previous runs alongside the current one.

githubArtifact.description: Upload as a workflow artifact. Convenient in CI but bounded by the repository retention window, so unsuitable as the system of record.

azureBlob.description: Durable evidence store. Recommended system of record. Write-once semantics are what make a pawprint evidence rather than a log, so immutability is enabled by default.

immutable.description: Apply a time-based retention policy so a written pawprint cannot be altered or deleted before it expires.

retentionDays.description: Immutability window. Choose to match your audit obligation; it cannot be shortened once locked.

redactBeforeUpload.description: Mask subscription, tenant, resource and operator identifiers before the pawprint leaves the runner.

admin.description: Identity configuration for the setup wizard and admin console. The public pawprint viewer has no auth and no backend; this section does not apply to it.

mode.description: entra: workforce tenant sign-in, recommended. local: generated credential bound to loopback, for air-gapped or no-Azure use. entra-external: CIAM tenant, advanced and generally discouraged for admin consoles.

tenantId.description: Directory the admin console authenticates against. Empty means auto-detect the tenant bound to the subscription.

clientId.description: Application (client) ID of the admin app registration. Not a secret.

authority.description: Authority host. Workforce tenants use login.microsoftonline.com; external tenants use <tenant>.ciamlogin.com.

credential.description: How the app proves its identity. Federated credentials and certificates are preferred; client secrets are discouraged and never stored in config.

requireAssignment.description: Only users or groups explicitly assigned to the application may sign in.

appRoles.description: Role names expected in the token. Authorization decisions read these claims.

bindAddress.description: Interface the local console binds to. Loopback is the default and changing it exposes the console to the network.

github.description: Optional GitHub App used to act on repositories. This is resource authorization, not a sign-in method.

scenarioCatalog.description: Path or repository reference to the scenario catalog.

ttlHours.description: Default lifetime for a run's resources before reaping. Impact: hot.

teardownOnFailure.description: Destroy provisioned resources when a run fails. Recommended true for ephemeral scenarios.

redactPawprint.description: Mask subscription, tenant, resource and operator identifiers in the emitted pawprint.

registry.description: Container registry for scenario images. 'ghcr' avoids provisioning an ACR.

parameters.description: Scenario parameter overrides, validated against the target scenario's own schema at preflight.

branch.description: Git branch bound to this environment. Deploying from a mismatched branch is a hard failure.

githubEnvironment.description: GitHub Environment name holding the OIDC identity variables.

subscriptionId.description: MUST remain an empty string. The real value is supplied at runtime from the AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID GitHub Environment variable, so a fork never commits a subscription identifier.

resourceGroup.description: Resource group for this environment. Impact: cold.

requireApproval.description: Whether this environment expects a GitHub Environment protection rule. Advisory; enforced by GitHub, asserted at preflight.
